items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: she was on the gig with us. So we had to accompany Ernestine without Hank.

ctx.x: So then my friend said he would send a private plane to pick him up in Albany and fly him down to Kennedy, and he didn’t show up. I get to Switzerland, I booked him in Switzerland to play with us. No Hank Jones. “Hank, what happened?” “Oh my car broke down on the way to the airport.” “Oh, Hank,” you know. Anyway, he finally showed up and strangely enough I’d booked him before in Toronto and he didn’t show up again. He claimed he couldn’t get out of here, out of New York, for the weather. And I got this guy Ian…

But fortunately we had Bucky. The reason he was booked, the guy wanted him of course, to play, Jones, but he’d made a record with Ernestine Anderson and she was on the gig with us. So we had to accompany Ernestine without Hank. He was the greatest pianist. Well he was another Dick Hyman, of that caliber. Oscar Peterson caliber. But he had that reputation, which was so sad.
I didn’t know that. You know he lived like an hour south of here.
